questions.def: Use past simple for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to the cinema last night.

questions.def: Use present perfect for a past action with present result.
questions.question: She ___ her keys. Now she can't open the door.

questions.def: Use 'is having' for arrangements. Use 'is going to have' or 'will have' instead.
questions.question: He is having a party next week.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for action started in the past.
questions.question: It ___ all morning.

questions.def: Present perfect for actions that started in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him since we were children.

questions.def: Past continuous for actions in progress at a specific time.
questions.question: When I arrived, they ___ dinner.

questions.def: 'Know' is a stative verb. Use 'know' instead of 'am knowing'.
questions.question: I am knowing the answer but won't tell.

questions.def: Past perfect for actions before another action in the past.
questions.question: He ___ in London before he moved to Rome.

questions.def: Past perfect shows an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: By the time I got there, the movie ___ already ___.

questions.def: Third conditional for hypothetical past situations.
questions.question: I ___ to the party if I had known you were going.

questions.def: Incorrect use of 'would' in the 'if' clause of a third conditional.
questions.question: If I would have known, I would helped.

questions.def: Past continuous for interrupted actions in the past.
questions.question: I ___ for the exam when you called.

questions.def: 'Was going to' for past intentions.
questions.question: She ___ be here at 8, but she's late.

questions.def: Present continuous for future arrangements.
questions.question: I ___ to Paris next week.

questions.def: Use the present perfect continuous ('has been living') with 'since'.
questions.question: She is living in London since 2010.

questions.def: Future perfect for actions completed by a time in the future.
questions.question: I ___ my work by 5 PM tomorrow.

questions.def: Simple present for habits and routines.
questions.question: I ___ to the gym every day.

questions.def: Past continuous for an action in progress in the past.
questions.question: He ___ his car when I saw him.

questions.def: Use the past simple ('played') to talk about a finished time.
questions.question: They are playing tennis yesterday afternoon.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for duration of an action.
questions.question: She ___ there since January.

questions.def: Present continuous for planned future events.
questions.question: They ___ to the beach next weekend.

questions.def: Past perfect for action before another in the past.
questions.question: Before she went to bed, she ___ her teeth.

questions.def: Use past simple for completed actions in past.
questions.question: He is playing football yesterday.

questions.def: Past continuous for an interrupted action.
questions.question: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.

questions.def: Use present perfect for past experiences.
questions.question: I ___ this movie before.

questions.def: Past continuous describes an action in progress at a past time.
questions.question: She ___ when the alarm clock went off.

questions.def: Use past simple for finished actions with a past time reference.
questions.question: He has went to Spain last year.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for duration of an action.
questions.question: They ___ for us for two hours.

questions.def: Use past simple after 'wish' to express a regret.
questions.question: I ___ that I would win the lottery!

questions.def: 'Would' is the past form of 'will' in reported speech.
questions.question: She said she ___ come to the party.
